input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only inspection right running against the Company. Notice (30 days' prior written notice), timing (Company's normal business hours) and cost (HDI bears its own inspection fees, unconditionally, which is better for us than the 5% carve-out) meet or exceed the playbook. However the clause has no frequency limit at all, the inspection is performed by HDI's own General Manager rather than an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and there is no express bar on direct access to Company systems. One concise inserted sentence supplies the annual frequency cap, the independent confidentiality-bound auditor and the no-system-access limit (which also keeps the exercise off our systems), leaving the favourable notice, business-hours and cost terms untouched.

ops.text: Any such inspection shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and shall not include any direct access to the Company's systems.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added the missing audit limits to Section 3.4 in one sentence: no more than one inspection in any twelve (12) month period, conducted by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and with no direct access to Company systems. The existing 30 days' notice, business-hours and HDI-bears-cost terms are acceptable as drafted.
proposal.summary: Add preferred audit limits: annual frequency, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, no system access
